stops.name: Berlin, the last light
stops.campa: Ninety years old, four volumes of Kosmos behind him and a fifth unfinished on the desk, Humboldt dies quietly in his rooms on the sixth of May. His last recorded words look, characteristically, outward and upward rather than at himself: how glorious these sunbeams, he says, as if the earth itself were being called up into the sky. All Berlin turns out for the funeral procession; he is carried to Tegel, to the family ground he left as a young man of twenty-nine to see the world, and laid beside the mother whose death, sixty-three years before, had set him free to go.
stops.quote: How glorious these sunbeams are! They seem to call Earth to the Heavens!
stops.quote_source: Reported last words, Berlin, 6 May 1859 (contemporary obituary tradition)
